    <span>2026.11</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout</h3>
  <p>Muir improves gated delta-rule linear attention by allocating lower-rank capacity to less sensitive erase gates, using matched-filter readout to reduce state interference, and introducing a stable parallel update. It improves language modeling and long-context recall over Gated DeltaNet-2 while matching its throughput.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08376" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="depthgraft-structural-regularization-through-hierarchical-cross-layer-kv-reconstruction">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.11</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction</h3>
  <p>DepthGraft reconstructs deep-layer keys and values from stride-aligned shallow and middle layers, using cross-layer KV reuse to distribute gradients and regularize KV representations. Across dense and MoE models, it improves downstream performance while reducing KV-cache storage by roughly one third and enabling earlier prefill completion.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03142" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Lookahead Sparse Attention, which uses a separately trained neural memory indexer to predict future context needs and retain only query-critical KV chunks on GPU. FlashMemory reduces the physical KV cache footprint to 13.5% of full-context attention on average while preserving or slightly improving long-context accuracy.</p>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>

  <h3>MiniMax Sparse Attention</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces MiniMax Sparse Attention, a blockwise sparse attention mechanism built on GQA that uses a lightweight Index Branch to select group-specific Top-k KV blocks before exact sparse attention. Co-designed GPU kernels turn the sparsity into large practical speedups at million-token context while maintaining performance close to dense GQA.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

<article class="paper-card" id="gqla-group-query-latent-attention-for-hardware-adaptive-large-language-model-decoding">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>GQLA: Group-Query Latent Attention for Hardware-Adaptive Large Language Model Decoding</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes Group-Query Latent Attention, a minimal MLA modification that exposes both MQA-absorb and GQA decoding paths from the same trained weights. The runtime can select the path that matches target hardware without retraining or custom kernels, enabling H100-style compressed decoding, H20-oriented GQA plus MTP, and up to 8-way zero-redundancy tensor parallelism.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15250" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.03</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Attention Residuals</h3>
  <p>This work replaces fixed residual accumulation with attention over previous layer outputs, enabling input-dependent depth-wise aggregation and reducing PreNorm-induced representation dilution. It also introduces Block AttnRes for scalable training with lower memory and communication overhead.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15031" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2025.10</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Kimi Linear, a hybrid architecture whose Kimi Delta Attention module combines fine-grained gating with an efficient chunkwise algorithm based on specialized diagonal-plus-low-rank transitions. A 48B-parameter model with 3B activated parameters outperforms full MLA under the same training recipe while reducing KV cache usage by up to 75% and delivering up to 6× decoding throughput at a 1M-token context.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2021.04</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>

  <h3>RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), which encodes absolute positions through rotations while making self-attention explicitly depend on relative positions. RoPE supports flexible sequence lengths, distance-aware dependency decay, and relative position encoding for linear self-attention.</p>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2019.11</span>
    <span>Attention Architecture</span>

  <h3>Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need</h3>
  <p>This paper introduces multi-query attention, sharing keys and values across attention heads to reduce the memory-bandwidth cost of incremental Transformer decoding. The variant speeds up decoding substantially while incurring only minor quality degradation relative to multi-head attention baselines.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

<article class="paper-card" id="a-broader-look-into-mllm-s-retrieval-heads">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.10</span>
    <span>Retrieval Heads</span>
  </div>
  <h3>A Broader Look into MLLM&#x27;s Retrieval Heads</h3>
  <p>Across 18 language, vision-language, and omni-modal checkpoints, this paper finds that a sparse set of retrieval attention heads is largely shared across modalities and retained during modality adaptation; ablating these heads sharply impairs audio-visual retrieval. Training their attention with a ranking objective improves Qwen3-VL-8B&#x27;s page Recall@1 on MMDocIR by 6.03 points.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32411" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
